green.note: Context only: trees and lawns are drawn from OpenStreetMap and are not counted as obstructions in the sun hours (canopies are seasonal and their heights are not surveyed).

census.source: NYC Street Tree Census 2015 (NYC Parks, uvpi-gqnh)
census.note: Context only: street trees are drawn from the NYC Street Tree Census (2015) and are not counted as obstructions in the sun hours (canopies are seasonal and porous). Canopy size is estimated from trunk diameter; the census does not record crown size. 65 census trees that the current NYC Parks inventory lists as removed (stump, retired or dead) are left out.

forestry.source: NYC Parks Forestry Tree Points (NYC Open Data, hn5i-inap)
forestry.note: Context only: park trees are drawn from the NYC Parks forestry inventory and are not counted as obstructions in the sun hours. Canopy size is estimated from trunk diameter; the inventory does not record crown size.

water.source: NYC Planimetric Database: Hydrography (NYC Open Data, pjs3-c3z5)
water.note: Context only: water is drawn from surveyed hydrography polygons (or OpenStreetMap outside New York) to show where the rivers and ponds are. It carries no tide, depth or current, and no sun or view number depends on it.

daylight_model.formula: DF_est % = T x Aw x theta / (A x (1 - R^2)) with theta = 90 deg x sky_view (BRE average daylight factor, Littlefair 1988; theta is the visible sky angle); defaults T 0.6, Aw 3.0 m2 glazing, A 88.6 m2 room surfaces (4 x 5 m, 2.7 m ceiling), R 0.5

sunshine.source: NOAA climate normals 1961-1990, percent of possible sunshine

daylight_annual.model: relative daylight model (modelled, not measured, not calibrated)

relative_daylight.unit: percent of the same sky's open horizontal illuminance
